title: 2nd Stopping Place 5th Truth The Indication Of Order In The Cosmos To Unity

questions.question: What does this passage mostly teach about Allah and the world?
questions.answer: Allah alone made and runs everything.

questions.question: What is seen all through the universe that points to this truth?
questions.answer: Careful order and regular patterns.

questions.question: Why does good order point to one Maker instead of many?
questions.answer: One ruler keeps things working together without conflict.

questions.question: What words in the passage show that Allah is the only One like this?
questions.answer: He is one, unique, and alone.

questions.question: What does the passage say Allah does not need from anyone?
questions.answer: He does not need a helper or partner.

questions.question: What does the passage say Allah does not have?
questions.answer: Weakness or نقص, meaning any lack or deficiency.

questions.question: The passage talks about the whole cosmos, its parts, and the beings in it. What do they all help prove?
questions.answer: They help prove Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What is special about many things in the world even though they are in many places?
questions.answer: They are alike in kind and follow the same plan.

questions.question: What does it mean that the same Divine Names and actions are at work in many places?
questions.answer: Allah’s power and care reach everywhere.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the earth like a home?
questions.answer: It calls it a beautiful palace.

questions.question: If one kind of rule and care is found everywhere, what can we understand?
questions.answer: One Lord is managing it all.

questions.question: Why is there no room for giving Allah partners in this passage?
questions.answer: Partners would bring disagreement, but the world shows one smooth order.

questions.question: Who is called the Maker, Disposer, Monarch, Nurturer, Master, and Builder in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: Why are so many titles used for Allah here?
questions.answer: To show He is in charge of everything in every way.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the order of the cosmos?
questions.answer: It is very complete and exact.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the things that help the world keep going?
questions.answer: They fit together and follow one shared plan.

questions.question: What can we learn from the same kinds of things being found in many places on earth?
questions.answer: One Creator spread them and controls them.

questions.question: What does “one within the other” help us picture?
questions.answer: Many things are mixed together but still work in order.

questions.question: If many mixed things still work neatly together, what does that show?
questions.answer: A wise and single Planner is in control.

questions.question: What is the meaning of saying Allah has no equal?
questions.answer: No one is like Him.

questions.question: What is the meaning of saying Allah has no opposite?
questions.answer: Nothing can stand against Him as a rival.

questions.question: What problem would happen if there were many gods running the world?
questions.answer: There would be fighting and disorder.

questions.question: What is one big sign in this passage that helps a believer trust Allah more?
questions.answer: The strong order seen everywhere.

questions.question: What stage is mentioned at the start of this truth?
questions.answer: The second stage.

questions.question: Who noticed this truth at that stage?
questions.answer: The traveler.

questions.question: What did the traveler notice in the whole universe?
questions.answer: Very fine order and regularity.

questions.question: Does the passage speak only about big things or also small parts?
questions.answer: It speaks about both the whole and the parts.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Divine Names and deeds in the world?
questions.answer: They reach and cover all or most things.

questions.question: Why is it important that the same kinds of actions are seen in every place?
questions.answer: It shows one Lord is acting everywhere.

questions.question: What does the spreading of elements and species over the earth help show?
questions.answer: That one Maker arranged them all.

questions.question: How is the world described to help us imagine it better?
questions.answer: Like a huge city and a decorated palace.

questions.question: What can a student infer when one style of care is seen in the whole world?
questions.answer: The same Creator is caring for all of it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah and partners?
questions.answer: Allah has no partners.

questions.question: Why does order itself become a proof in this passage?
questions.answer: Because true order needs one organizer.

questions.question: What is the clearest main idea of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The ordered universe clearly shows Allah is One.

questions.question: What does the passage say is found in all of the cosmos?
questions.answer: Strong order and sameness in how things are run.

questions.question: What does “regularity” mean here in simple words?
questions.answer: Things happen in a steady, organized way.

questions.question: The passage compares the world to a palace. What does that comparison help us understand?
questions.answer: The world is arranged on purpose, not by accident.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah needing a minister or aide?
questions.answer: He does not need any.

questions.question: What does it mean that Allah is sole?
questions.answer: He is alone in His rule.

questions.question: What kind of things in the world are said to be alike and spread widely?
questions.answer: Elements and species.

questions.question: Why is sameness across many places important in the passage?
questions.answer: It points to one source and one command.

questions.question: What happens to peace and order when people imagine partners with Allah, according to the passage?
questions.answer: That would lead to dispute and confusion.

questions.question: Which is a better match for this passage: “many rulers” or “one ruler”?
questions.answer: One ruler.

questions.question: What can we learn about Allah’s power from this passage?
questions.answer: His power reaches the whole universe.

questions.question: What faith lesson should a Muslim child take from this passage?
questions.answer: We should believe Allah alone made, owns, and manages everything.

questions.question: What is being proved in this Fifth Truth?
questions.answer: The oneness of Allah.

questions.question: What are two signs in the universe that help prove this?
questions.answer: Order and things working in the same way.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the cosmos, its pillars, its parts, and its beings?
questions.answer: To show the proof is everywhere.

questions.question: What does it mean that many things follow a general scheme?
questions.answer: They fit into one big plan.

questions.question: What can we understand when the same kinds of elements are found across the earth?
questions.answer: One Lord spread them and governs them.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah having a peer?
questions.answer: He has none.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah having any deficiency?
questions.answer: He has none.

questions.question: Why can’t perfect order come from many equal rulers?
questions.answer: They would not keep everything united in one peaceful system.

questions.question: What does the word “demands” help us understand in this passage?
questions.answer: The signs strongly require us to see one Maker.

questions.question: What is the cause in this passage, and what is the result?
questions.answer: The cause is the perfect order in creation; the result is knowing Allah is One.

questions.question: How does this passage help someone answer, “Who runs the world?”
questions.answer: Allah alone runs it.

questions.question: What short belief statement fits this whole passage?
questions.answer: Allah is One and has no partner.

questions.question: What big truth is the passage trying to make clear?
questions.answer: The whole universe shows Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the things inside the universe?
questions.answer: They are arranged with great order.

questions.question: Are the same Divine actions limited to one small place in the passage?
questions.answer: No. They are shown everywhere.

questions.question: What does that teach us about Allah’s care?
questions.answer: His care covers all things.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention a city and a palace?
questions.answer: To help us picture a place that is ruled and arranged.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah and helpers?
questions.answer: He does not need helpers.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah and weakness?
questions.answer: He has no weakness.

questions.question: What is one clue from nature that supports this teaching?
questions.answer: The same order appears throughout the world.

questions.question: Why is arguing for many gods against the message of this passage?
questions.answer: Because many gods would bring division, but creation shows unity.

questions.question: What should a child think when seeing the world work in a neat way?
questions.answer: Allah wisely made it all and controls it.

questions.question: Finish the idea in a simple way: Since creation is orderly and united, therefore…
questions.answer: Allah is the one and only Lord.
